📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1345 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Climbing ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: How My First Multi-Pitch Climb Became a Midnight Barefoot Epic

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1345 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Climbing

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that on July 4, 2026, Audrey Callaway climbed her first real multi-pitch: Diedre (5.8, 6 pitches) in Squamish, B.C.
  • After first getting into the sport at a gym in Chicago, Callaway later moved to upstate New York near the Gunks.
  • According to recent reports, callaway wanted to share her experience to highlight the growing pains of “doing things poorly the first time”—and how the right partners ease those pains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on July 4, 2026, Audrey Callaway climbed her first real multi-pitch: Diedre (5.8, 6 pitches) in Squamish, B.C. The catch? She didn’t start up pitch one until nearly 9 p.m., thus becoming voluntarily benighted in only the most literal sense of the term. “My story isn’t a disaster!” Callaway explains. “It’s about learning, the tenacity of a little psych, and extremely good company.”.

After first getting into the sport at a gym in Chicago, Callaway later moved to upstate New York near the Gunks. Currently, she’s studying forestry at the University of Vermont. “I like trees, I like climbing, I like birds,” she says of her big three hobbies. She’s mostly a boulderer and sport climber who wants to get more into trad climbing. She also works at a climbing gym.

According to recent reports, callaway wanted to share her experience to highlight the growing pains of “doing things poorly the first time”—and how the right partners ease those pains. Below, she shares her story and what others embarking on their first multi-pitch can learn from her experience.

It’s really cool to feel very bad at something again.

I was planning to visit my girlfriend Lucy, who had been in Squamish for the whole summer. Then my best friend Will, who I grew up climbing with at the gym, told me he also happened to be going out to Squamish. I got there a few days before him and did a little bouldering.

Industry observers note that when Will got there, he was even more psyched than I was. After bouldering all afternoon, we’re sitting around, playing chess and looking through Lucy’s guidebook when we saw a trad climb that looked so cool: Diedre (5.8, 6 pitches).

In a recent development, it was 7 p.m., but the sun didn’t set until around 9 p.m. It was very spur of the moment. We’re just like, “We gotta do this thing.” So we swiftly got all our stuff together.

Industry observers note that we knew it was going to get dark. It’s not like it snuck up on us. But Lucy had a lot of experience. Will and I didn’t know how to trad climb at this point, although he learned later on that trip. So she’s carrying the team. Afterward, she told me she brought only a single rack so that she could share in our sense of adventure and “empathize with the uncertainty.”.

First, we got super lost on the way there. We didn’t get to the base of the climb until like 8:45 p.m., but it was still super bright out.

It has been revealed that very rapidly, I realized how bad I was at rope management. I was in the middle, belaying Lucy, and we had two ropes. Routefinding is something that you take for granted when you’ve been climbing outside for a while. I was taking the path of most resistance. There was a pretty solid crack on really good terrain, but I’m newer to crack climbing, so I was not about to put my hands in there and trust that. Instead, I was doing this very sketchy 5.10 slab. Eventually, I started using the crack.

According to recent reports, we got up to the first belay and we’re all on top of each other because we don’t really know where to be. Nothing was unsafe, but it was very slow. Lucy started going up this 5.6 very runout slab. But I had looped a knot of rope around where I was belaying. I didn’t realize that until I’d fed out enough of the slack. So I kept shorting her like every five feet. I knew that there was totally a way to fix this, but I don’t know how.

Recent findings suggest that then the sun set. That’s okay, because we had headlamps—but Lucy’s headlamp was dead. It was funny because before we started climbing, Lucy was like, “Guys, make sure you have your headlamps.” But then when we put them on, she’s like, “Can I actually borrow yours?”.

So she took mine, and now I was climbing in the dark on slab. It was very precarious, but beautiful. It felt so scary in the moment. But the town was right there, we’re on the most classic 5.8 ever, and we’re a hundred feet off the ground—it wasn’t actually that scary.

It has been revealed that will and I both had super competitive shoes on. It had been two hours at this point and we’re standing on this slab and our feet were killing us. Every time I left the belay, Will told me he “would lowkey start crying a bit” because he knew he’d have to climb soon, enduring more toe pain. So we both took off our shoes because it’s easier to climb barefoot. Now I was barefoot in the dark on this slab.

Every time we got to a newly introduced belay, we tried to make the system better. Lucy was just trying to climb, but we’re shorting her every time. Now Will was in the way. We were right on top of each other.

In a recent development, none of these things were particularly hard challenges. If we knew what we were doing, we could have fixed any one of these problems in 30 seconds. I would get back up to Lucy and she would be like, “Why didn’t you just do this?” Then something else would come up.

Recent findings suggest that at one point, probably around 11:30 p.m., Will got a cam stuck. Lucy’s like, “Try wiggling it.” She told him to pull upward, but he said it was literally impossible. Lucy lowered down and pulled it out, first try. There must have been times like this when Lucy was frustrated, but she never showed it. Will describes Lucy as the most patient person he’s ever met.

Industry observers note that we got to the top at midnight. It was hypnotizing on the apron. The lights of town beneath us glowed surreally. I smoked my first cigarette at the top.

It has been revealed that I remember walking back and it was really quiet. We got back on the road and our gear’s rattling and the moon’s out. It was so quiet and peaceful.

It was one in the morning when we got back to the campground by the Chief. We didn’t want to be disrespectful with a substantial light, so we put a headlamp under this pickle jar we had. By the light of this pickle lamp, we ate pickles and cold canned minestrone and asked, “What are we gonna do tomorrow?”.

In a recent development, to really be benighted, I would say it has to sneak up on you. It kinda felt like it snuck up on me. Clearly, as a group we were aware it was about to happen. But I was surprised when all of a sudden it was dark and I had no headlamp and was climbing barefoot. It made me feel like a salamander, really in touch with the rock.

Lucy and I did another multi-pitch the next day, and since then I’ve done a couple two-pitch climbs in the Gunks when I got back to New York. I will probably do lots of really awesome multi-pitches in my lifetime that are beautiful and scenic with really hard climbing, but I’m never gonna have another one that bad. I’m never gonna have another first one.

As told to Maya Silver. This story has been edited for length, structure, and clarity.

The Best Stretches to Reduce Quad Pain After a Hard Ski Run, According to a Physical Therapist

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (709 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Outsideonline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that having sore quads after skiing might seem like a side effect reserved for beginners who pizza their way down the slopes.
  • Even with good form, your quads are the dominant muscle in skiing—especially the lateral quad (vastus lateralis), which is the most active when you turn, James Spencer, a physical therapist in Aspen, Colorado, told Outside.
  • The root cause behind this soreness is the same reason your legs are tender after an arduous trail run or a lower-body weightlifting workout.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that having sore quads after skiing might seem like a side effect reserved for beginners who pizza their way down the slopes. But athletes of all levels can suffer from them.

Even with good form, your quads are the dominant muscle in skiing—especially the lateral quad (vastus lateralis), which is the most active when you turn, James Spencer, a physical therapist in Aspen, Colorado, told Outside. The stronger a skier you are, the harder you can push your quads on the mountain, which means “you can find a way to make them sore, no matter your skiing level,” he explained.

The root cause behind this soreness is the same reason your legs are tender after an arduous trail run or a lower-body weightlifting workout. When you intensely and repeatedly load your quads, you create microscopic tears in the muscle fibers. That damage may sound bad, but it’s actually a good thing: it’s one of the triggers that tells your body to strengthen that muscle, Spencer noted.

Still, the side effects can be unpleasant. As with any bodily injury, the microtears trigger swelling, which increases the pain you feel after exercise and causes that sore sensation, Spencer explains. Officially known as delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS), this feeling sets in after your workout ends and can peak as late as two to three days after. So if you feel fine boarding the shuttle at the end of a long ski day, but find yourself hobbling to the toilet the next morning, DOMS is probably the culprit.

The true cure for DOMS is time. “You really just gotta wait for those [microtears] to heal,” Spencer said. But there’s also something you can do in the interim to ease your pain slightly: quad stretches.

By gently stretching your quads after a hard day on the mountain, you can decrease the intensity of your soreness by flushing out some of the inflammation in your muscles, Spencer said. It won’t be a cure-all, but it can help you move and feel better in the short term. Read on for the specific moves Spencer recommends.

Sources indicate that you don’t need a ton of quad stretches to find relief. In fact, Spencer claims two are enough. You’ve probably seen these stretches before, and while, sure, they’re not the most exciting, they are simple and effective.

Optional: Do this stretch in a hot tub. The heat may also help reduce feelings of soreness.

The above stretches can be sufficient to help reduce quad soreness, but if you’re looking for more, Spencer also suggests other recovery methods.

Industry observers note that spend a couple of minutes foam rolling your quads, including the front of your thigh (from the knee all the way up to the hip) and the sides to hit the vastus lateralis (basically where your IT band is). Similar to stretching, foam rolling can bring some relief to the quads by reducing swelling in the area.

Another option: hop on a stationary bike and gently cycle your legs for ten to 15 minutes. This easy movement can also reduce soreness by pumping out inflammation from your quads, Spencer mentioned. Just make sure to keep the resistance and your effort level low. “It’s not meant to be a workout,” he said.

Stretches can ease DOMS in the short term, but if you want to prevent intense soreness altogether, strengthening your quads is the ticket.

Recent findings suggest that “If you just build a little strength going into the season, you’re going to be less sore,” Spencer remarked. And you’re also less likely to get injured, he added.

Exercises such as quad sets, wall sits, and really any squat variation like traditional squats, Bulgarian split squats, and single-leg squats can all strengthen the muscle group.

“The thing I hear all the time is the only way to get ready for skiing is by skiing, and that’s a total lie,” Spencer remarked. There’s a lot you can do both in the off-season and throughout the winter to prime your body for the demands of skiing, he said. In addition to quad-strengthening exercises, he recommends hamstring, glute, and core moves, plus jumping exercises that train your ability to react to the unexpected.

#102106. Hike of the Week: Explore the Dramatic—and Threatened—Big Bend on This Desert Peak

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (700 w)

Hike of the Week: Explore the Dramatic—and Threatened—Big Bend on This Desert Peak

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (700 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Backpacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The first time I visited Santa Elena Canyon, the gorge in Big Bend National Park that straddles the border between the U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that nine years later, Significant Bend is still beautiful.
  • Recent findings suggest that one of the best ways to see it today is the hike up Emory Peak.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

(Photo: kellyvandellen/Getty Images).

The first time I visited Santa Elena Canyon, the gorge in Big Bend National Park that straddles the border between the U.S. and Mexico, I was amazed not just at how beautiful it was, but how peaceful. The buff and black-streaked limestone walls soared 1,500 feet over the water, the afternoon sun streaming through the gap. The river was running low and slow, trickling over the mud and rocks, no more than knee deep. I rolled up my pant legs and waded into the water, toward that invisible line in the middle of the river that split two countries.

Recent findings suggest that nine years later, Significant Bend is still beautiful. Covering an area bigger than Rhode Island, this stretch of West Texas desert is home to some of the state’s most moving scenery, from river canyons to rocky peaks, with animal and plant life to match. Hikers willing to put in the work on the area’s rugged trails may spot javelinas rooting in the undergrowth or nocturnal, raccoon-like ringtails climbing up the cliffs and trees of the Chisos Mountains; they’ll see prickly pear cactus and ocotillo, a spindly, Seussian shrub equipped with vicious spines, growing wild in the desert flats. (That border, however, may soon be far more concrete. Read on for more on that.).

Recent findings suggest that one of the best ways to see it today is the hike up Emory Peak. At 7,825 feet, Emory is the highest point in Big Bend and the Chisos, and enjoys commanding views of the terrain for miles around. Getting there, however, takes some muscle: The rough, 9.7-mile hike to the top ascends singletrack and rock stairs through oak, piñon, and juniper forest before ending with a final, dramatic scramble to the peak’s exposed summit. November, when summer’s broiling temperatures finally cool down, is an ideal time to hike it. (Note: There is no water at all along the Emory Peak Trail, and the NPS suggests hikers carry at least one liter per person per hour.).

Sources indicate that the round trip takes about 6 to 8 hours, and you’ll want to leave some time to relax afterward. Santa Elena Canyon’s picnic area is an ideal spot for an early dinner, and cap off the night at the park’s free riverside hot springs. (Due to recent flood damage, reaching both of these highlights is at the moment harder than usual. The paved road between Cottonwood Campground and Santa Elena is closed at the time of writing; drivers with a true 4-wheel drive vehicle and high clearance can get there on Old Maverick Road. Due to another closure, getting to the hot springs requires a 4-mile round-trip, relatively flat hike along a gravel road. Consider it part of the adventure.).

In a recent development, starting at the Chisos Basin Visitors Center, take the Laguna Meadows trail for about a third of a mile to a fork, where you’ll hang a left on the Pinnacles Trail. Follow it as it steadily climbs, traversing desert flats and rocky slopes with the sheer top of Emory looming in the background. After another 3.4 miles, the trail reaches a saddle below the top of the peak. Continue on the Emory Peak Trail for another 1.5 miles, then tackle a final, somewhat exposed 30-foot scramble to the top of the mountain and 360-degree views of the park below. Retrace your steps to the trailhead, or break up the hike by reserving one of the Pinnacles campsites ahead of your trip.

In a recent development, in an 8-1 decision on November 9, the Supreme Court approved a request by the Trump administration to resume construction of a border wall through Big Bend, ruling against plaintiffs who had argued that the barrier would decimate rare plant species and cut off migratory routes for animals, and that it risked damaging ancient rock art and Native heritage sites. In Santa Elena Canyon itself, the Department of Homeland Security aims to install vehicle barriers and surveillance infrastructure and clear patrol roads through the area. Conservation groups and state officials like Governor-Elect Gina Hinojosa say they’ll continue to push to end construction in the park.

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (359 w)

Unequipped Hikers Rescued from Winter Storm on Colorado Section of the Continental Divide Trail

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (359 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Backpacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Snow on the mountains above Rollins Pass, Colorado.
  • A late fall hike turned into an overnight rescue on the Colorado section of the Continental Divide Trail on November 14 when a trio of hikers called for a rescue after encountering severe weather and wintry conditions at 11,600 feet.
  • Located about an hour and a half drive away from Denver, the High Lonesome Trail runs concurrent with part of the CDT, reaching a high point of 12,111 feet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Snow on the mountains above Rollins Pass, Colorado. (Photo: SWKrullImaging via Getty).

A late fall hike turned into an overnight rescue on the Colorado section of the Continental Divide Trail on November 14 when a trio of hikers called for a rescue after encountering severe weather and wintry conditions at 11,600 feet.

Located about an hour and a half drive away from Denver, the High Lonesome Trail runs concurrent with part of the CDT, reaching a high point of 12,111 feet. When hiked in its entirety, it also involves 3,742 feet of elevation gain over the course of 18 miles. Recent day-time temperature highs in the area have hovered between 26 and 37 degrees, while lows were recorded at 5 and 9 degrees with wind gusts as high as 50 mph.

Grand County Search and Rescue (GCSAR), which responded, mentioned that the hikers called for help after encountering dangerous trail conditions, significant snow, and navigational struggles. The team dispatched a group of rescuers who rode ATVs up the Rollins Pass Road before dismounting and hiking the remaining distance there. When rescuers made it to the trio, they found the hikers were wet, cold, and tired.

In a recent development, “The subjects had set up camp but lacked appropriate gear, including fire making supplies, to spend the night in the deteriorating weather,” rescue officials wrote. A second rescue team joined the party later in the evening before accompanying the hikers back to the staged ATVs and from there to the trailhead.

Recent findings suggest that although most of Grand County has yet to see significant snow, November can be a deceptive time of the year to hike in Colorado’s high country. Trails may appear accessible, but factors like extreme temperatures, inclement weather and reduced daylight hours can make hiking and camping more treacherous than usual.

It has been revealed that the Continental Divide Trail is the highest-elevation long trail in the United States, with its high point at the summit of 14,278-foot Grays Peak. Colorado’s section is the highest on the trail; the USFS estimates that the CDT’s average elevation across the state is 10,000 feet.

#102096. Latest Update: Adrian Ballinger Is Returning to Mount Everest’s South Side. Here’s Why.

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1006 w)

Latest Update: Adrian Ballinger Is Returning to Mount Everest’s South Side. Here’s Why.

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1006 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Outsideonline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ballinger, founder of Alpenglow Expeditions, is a veteran of Mount Everest climbing (Photo: Griffinf Mims).
  • For more than a decade, American expedition leader Adrian Ballinger swore off guiding climbers up Mount Everest’s popular South Col route in Nepal.
  • In interviews, Ballinger noted the crowds, the trash, the ever-present problem with human waste, and the frequency of rescues and deaths along the route.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ballinger, founder of Alpenglow Expeditions, is a veteran of Mount Everest climbing (Photo: Griffinf Mims).

For more than a decade, American expedition leader Adrian Ballinger swore off guiding climbers up Mount Everest’s popular South Col route in Nepal.

In interviews, Ballinger noted the crowds, the trash, the ever-present problem with human waste, and the frequency of rescues and deaths along the route. Atop his list of concerns, however, was the deadly Khumbu Icefall, the site of avalanches and dangerous crumbling seracs. Every spring, Sherpa porters and guides must make dozens of trips through the crumbling glacier to ferry food, tents, and oxygen to higher camps.

According to recent reports, “If you run 20 trips on Everest over the next 20 years and hire 15 to 20 Sherpas each year, you’re putting a lot of people’s lives in danger,” Ballinger told Outside in a 2023 interview. “We don’t feel that we can run an ethical expedition from the south side.”.

Sources indicate that ballinger’s firm, Alpenglow Expeditions, led a handful of trips to Everest’s south side in the aughts. But starting in 2014, Alpenglow exclusively led Everest trips from the mountain’s northern side in Tibet, which is controlled by China.

Industry observers note that now, Ballinger is taking steps to return to Everest’s southern side. In a recent interview, he told Outside that his three-year strategy for Alpenglow is to lead trips up Everest from both Tibet and Nepal concurrently.

“Even though we still think the north side of Everest is better for our clients, we are considering the south side as a backup,” Ballinger said. “And ultimately, we hope to be able to run trips on both sides of the mountain, provided we get the approvals that we expect.”.

Returning to Nepal gives Alpenglow a backup initiative in case China closes the peak to climbers, Ballinger said.

Industry observers note that climbers tackling Everest from the northern side of the China-Nepal border enjoy a few advantages, namely smaller crowds and a Base Camp accessible by vehicles. But the Chinese government’s repeated decision to close Everest with little warning has stymied expedition leaders. In 2008, China closed Everest just weeks before the climbing season to allow the Olympic torch relay to ascend the peak.

Industry observers note that since 2016, China has shuttered Everest five additional times. It closed the peak in 2020 due to the Covid pandemic, and kept Everest off-limits through the 2023 season. Ballinger returned the following year with an expedition to the top.

In a recent development, “We had incredible seasons on Everest in 2024 and 2025, some of the best of my life,” Ballinger said. “It was uncrowded, we had great support from the Chinese, and it was totally open.”.

In 2026, Ballinger and other guides were preparing for another successful season on Everest’s north side when China abruptly canceled the season in early March. The decision came painfully late in the season. Expedition operators had already promised paychecks to guides and mountain workers. And climbers usually arrive at Base Camps in China and Nepal in mid-April.

Industry observers note that “We took the financial losses and did the right thing,” Ballinger said. “We paid our Sherpas and our guides and our workers who waited until the end. We ate that cost.”.

Ballinger remarked he then gave his climbing clients refunds or deferrals to the 2027 season. One-third accepted deferrals to 2027, while two-thirds booked with other outfitters in Nepal in 2026, he said. Alpenglow helped its clients find expeditions to join on Everest’s south side for the 2026 season.

According to recent reports, “Financially it’s not easy,” Ballinger remarked. “It definitely sucks, but we want the best for our clients.”.

Operating in both Nepal and Tibet, however, would allow Alpenglow to shift clients from one side of the peak to the other in the instance of a closure.

“Between 2007 and this year—that’s 20 seasons—we’ve had to cancel six times,” he noted. “In those years there’s a lot of stress.”.

Ballinger cited the rapid introduction of cargo-carrying drones on Everest’s south side as another reason for his decision to return. In 2026, a organization called Airlift Technologies began ferrying gear and supplies from Base Camp at 17,500 feet over the Khumbu Icefall up to Camp I at 19,900 feet via heavy-duty cargo drones.

Alpenglow’s lead guide, Esteban “Topo” Mena, spent time at the Nepali Base Camp in 2026 to watch the business grow.

According to recent reports, “We sent Topo to check out the scene and see if he thought the experimentation that’s going on with drone technology had a meaningful impact,” Ballinger mentioned. “We think we can replace all of our Sherpa carries through the Khumbu Icefall with drones.”.

Each drone delivery to Camp I eliminates a human trip through the Khumbu Icefall. In 2026, several Everest outfitters relied heavily on Airlift Technologies’ drone service to transport gear above Base Camp.

Industry observers note that the drone business grew out of two seasons of testing. Starting in 2024, Nepali drone companies began completing test flights of heavy-duty cargo drones amid the thin air at Everest Base Camp. In 2025, drone pilots successfully flew an oxygen canister and bags of gear from Base Camp to Camp I, proving the potential for a drone business.

The drone business is not without its problems. In 2026, the Nepali government grounded Airlift Technologies’ drones for four days without explanation.

Piloting a cargo drone over the Khumbu Icefall requires skill and technological innovation. One pilot at Base Camp controls the drone at takeoff. But when the craft reaches a specific elevation, a second pilot at Camp I takes over control, navigating the craft past towers of ice and sheer rock walls to land it on the upper flanks of the Khumbu Glacier.

“We see it as a really exciting change,” Ballinger said. “We’ve been talking for years now about what would allow the icefall to become manageable in the long term. We think drones are a stepping stone in that direction.”.

Industry News: How to Make a Handprint Calendar

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (600 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tinybeans

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, hanging around the house for the holidays?
  • Recent findings suggest that we love this project because there’s no right way to make one.
  • Related: How to Make a Vision Board for Kids in 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hanging around the house for the holidays? Spend an afternoon or two working on a handprint calendar for 2027. It’s an easy project anyone can complete, and little helpers will love to lend a hand or two. After all, you’ve got a long winter break to fill with activities and printables, and by Newly introduced Year’s Eve, you’ll have reached the point where painting your kids’ hands sounds like a rational idea!

Recent findings suggest that we love this project because there’s no right way to make one. Keep it simple, or get super crafty— it’s all up to your kids’ imagination. Use the guide below to get started, and decide in advance what you’ll make out of each handprint. This is much easier to do before your little helper has paint all over their hands!

Related: How to Make a Vision Board for Kids in 2027.

Paint your kids’ hands with the selected colors and have them make a print on each piece of paper. Colored paper is also an option if you want to use white paint (see January and October). Depending on your design, you may need just one handprint, a fingerprint, or even a footprint. Be sure to wash and dry your hands between each month, and continue through the year, from January to December. If you think it doesn’t look like much, don’t worry! After each month has dried, and you add the details, it’ll look awesome.

Insider Tip: Let your kids have some input with this project. While you may have a perfect vision in mind for how to execute a gorgeous Christmas tree using their sweet little hands, they might have another idea, and that’s okay.

Recent findings suggest that now that you have all of the months ready to go (and dry!), it’s time to put your calendar together. The easiest way to go is to order a ready-made blank calendar, such as this blank wall calendar from Amazon. For under $10, you won’t have to mess with binding or stapling, or fussing with the assembly of the calendar—glue or use double-sided tape to attach your own homemade monthly pictures to the blank template and you’re good to go.

Related: Upcoming Year’s Eve Confetti Poppers You Can Make with the Kids.

Print out a blank 2023 calendar from Calendar Labs. One by one, place the pages behind the handprint so that when it flips upward, you’ll have the right picture and month. For example, the calendar days for January should be glued to the February picture, the calendar days for February should be glued to March, and so on.

Insider Tip: Make sure to place the calendar month on the backside and bottom of the handprint, so as you flip each month, the painted picture is positioned the correct way.

Once you’ve glued all the calendar pages to the handprints, use the laminating sleeves to seal each one. Follow the instructions on the package, and use a ruler to eliminate any air pockets or creases.

Using a hole punch, make three holes at the top of each page (the calendar month should have the holes at the top) and one hole at the bottom (this is where the calendar will hang on the wall).

In a recent development, then, using string or thin twine, run a length through each of the three holes and tie it up like you would a book (it should open from the right side). That’s it! You’ll have a fun keepsake that will hang around for an entire year.

Sleep-Unders Are Honestly a Win for Everyone

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (299 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tinybeans

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As soon as kids hit school age, the pressure of the sleepover begins.
  • It has been revealed that the sleep-under brings the best elements of the sleepover and avoids the actual sleeping-over part.
  • All the festivities are concluded just before bedtime, when parents return to swoop up their little ones and everyone heads back home to sleep in their own beds.

As soon as kids hit school age, the pressure of the sleepover begins. Whether your little one wants to host a crew of first graders in your living room (hard pass) or is being asked to sleep over at someone else’s house, there are a lot of questions that come with the milestone. Will my kid have fun? Will they sleep at all? Will they be overwhelmed? Add to that concerns surrounding safety, and it’s a tough position for parents to be in. The solution: the “sleep-under.”.

It has been revealed that the sleep-under brings the best elements of the sleepover and avoids the actual sleeping-over part. It’s become a trendy birthday party theme because it puts less pressure on kids and the parents hosting. How it works is that kids show up to the host house all ready for a sleepover, usually around dinner time. Guests might even arrive decked out in their coziest PJs to add to the whole sleepover vibe. The group enjoys pizza, watches a movie, plays some games, and does an activity like decorating cupcakes.

All the festivities are concluded just before bedtime, when parents return to swoop up their little ones and everyone heads back home to sleep in their own beds. Nobody is over-tired the next day. Nobody needs to call home for a late-night pickup when they have a nightmare. No parent has to stress over whether it’s a good idea to leave their kid overnight with someone they only know from the pick-up line. No kid has to feel ashamed if they aren’t yet ready to sleep away from their parents for the night. The sleep-under side-steps all those potential issues.

Honestly, it’s pretty genius. We just wish it were a thing when we were kids!

Between daily parenting duties, work, and navigating the current world in general, saying your days are full is probably an understatement. And while your kid’s day may be full of exploration and creativity, they can also experience a lot of anxiety, stress, and pressure. That makes it even more crucial to have some positive, uninterrupted time to reconnect.

It has been revealed that even five minutes can make a difference in a child’s emotional well-being. But as Randy McCoy, VP of Product & Curriculum for The Little Gym, reminds us, how long you play is less crucial than how often. “It’s not necessarily the ‘duration of play’ but the ‘frequency of play’ that matters most,” Mccoy says. “If a parent can give their child their undivided attention and play with them just five minutes a day, every day, they’re on the right track.”.

The good news is, there are lots of ways to play that take next-to-no prep. Read on for 21 easy ideas to play with your kids, whether you have five minutes, 15, or more.

When you have a few minutes, whether it’s before school or after dinner, bust out these little-to-no-prep basics you can use just about anywhere.

Sources indicate that 1. Try out “Would You Rather?” kid edition. Spend a fun five minutes taking turns asking questions like, “Would you rather never eat ice cream again or get a trampoline?” or “Ride a dinosaur for 20 miles or an elephant for an hour?” The sillier the better. This also makes a great road trip game.

2. Make a dictionary dash. Grab a dictionary and choose a word at random. Read it out loud and have the kids guess what it means. If they can read, they can take turns finding words and trying to stump you.

Recent findings suggest that 3. Tickle your sidekick’s funny bone. Whip out brain busters or riddles that will make them laugh. Luckily, you don’t need Comedy Central writers for this one. We think your goofballs will get a kick out of our ultimate list of jokes for kids.

4. A few rounds of “We’re going on a picnic” alphabet-style will entertain the tot lot. The first player up says, “I’m going on a picnic,” then adds a tasty packable to the phrase, like an apple, apricot, or avocado. Stick with ABC order or focus on just one letter for each round.

Sources indicate that 5. Play 20 questions. Have your kids guess what you’re thinking of, and keep it simple, like something you can see from where you’re standing.

6. Play a classic game of Rock, Paper, Scissors—Japanese style. It’s called Janken. Start by saying “saisho wa guu.” Then “janken pon” as you pump, before throwing on “pon.” The winning combos are still the same in this timeless, quick game you can play at home or on the go.

7. Turn yourself into a living “spot the difference” puzzle. Start with a slow model turn, then disappear and make a quick change out of sight. When you come back, your cutie’s got to spot what’s different. Did you take off a cap? Put on a scarf? Untie a shoe? Keep it easy for the tots, and kick it up a notch for older kiddos (only one earring!). Then let them have a turn trying to stump you.

Recent findings suggest that 8. Try out a sequencing game when the wanderlust takes hold. Name a person, place, and object, all starting with the same letter of the alphabet, then string them together like kids lining up for the school bus. “Alice from Australia loves alligators!” See how far you can get in a short amount of time.

For parents, playing with our kids allows us to step out of all those daily parental duties and, as McCoy explains, build friendship between parent and child. “It provides an opportunity for you to interact with them on a different level,” he indicates. “For a special moment, you step out of the ‘parent’ role and step into a playmate role.”  Take a break from your to-do list and try one of these 15-minute ideas that will thrill the kids and relax you, too.

9. Post-It style. A stack of Post-It notes and a pen are all it takes to play this short-and-sweet variation of the classic guessing game for parties. Choose someone to be “it.” Write on the Post-It note the name of a character from a book, movie, or show that your kid will recognize—it can be a famous person, someone they know, or a fictional character. Stick the note to their forehead, without letting them see what you wrote. Now take turns going around the room giving “it” clues to help them guess who is on their head.

It has been revealed that 10. Curl up with a good book. Putting out a basket of books in a central location motivates the kids to take a look through the pages when they’ve got time to spare. Add in a sweet bookmark that keeps track of time to make it count.

11. Give them their daily feels. Keep your favorite sensory bin fillers on hand (like cotton balls and dry beans), along with trinkets to bury and cups for spilling and filling. When you’ve got a short window, pull out the bin, fill ‘er up, and watch your kids dig and drizzle until it’s time to go.

12. Set up a quick cotton ball and straw race. Perfect for the kitchen table before lunch is served. Have siblings challenge each other for the pole position on a straightaway down the center of the table, or set up a simple obstacle course using cups that the kiddos have to work around. Ready, set, go!

Recent findings suggest that 13. Give a penny for their thoughts when they write in a journal. Setting aside a short amount of time to write (each day!) is a great way to encourage your amateur author’s creativity. Use silly or thought-provoking prompts to get them thinking, like, “The first time I tried …” or “When I get to be principal, I’ll …” or even “The craziest thing that happened today…” Write on, brother!

Industry observers note that 14. Give up the charade. Have your little monkey stay in character when you play a quick game of animal charades. No prep is necessary for this easy guessing game. Just pick your favorite animal and go for it! With each successful guess, trade places and start again. Ee-i-ee-i-o!

According to recent reports, whether your aim is active playtime or quiet(er) crafting time, filling a cool 30 minutes with your kids is easier than you think. It may take a bit of planning, but once the prep is done, it’s a sit-back-and-relax situation that’s well worth the time upfront.

15. All things LEGO. If LEGO was the first thing that popped into your head, then we’re right there with you. They’re the forever fallback for a reason, but to hit that half-hour sweet spot, try throwing a LEGO challenge into the mix: building a car that can also work underwater, or constructing a tower that’s at least 24 inches tall. Then let your master-builder go to work.

Recent findings suggest that 16. Spin them right round. Ana at Babble Dabble Do has a latest way to play with Perler beads. She puts them to work teaching science and playing tricks when these melted beauties become spinning tops. It’s just the right amount of make-and-play to fill a brief window in your busy day.

In a recent development, 17. One for the movers and shakers. Print out (and laminate if you’re feeling bold) The Alerting Activity Game, designed by Training Happy Hearts. Keep the deck on hand to stack the odds in your favor when the kids need something to do. With simple activities like “jump up and down ten times” or “pretend to be a volcano,” it’s packed with energy-burning activities that kids can run through on their own or with you!

18. Bring the outside in and paint it. If snow isn’t covering your yard, go for a hunt for leaves, evergreen boughs, and sticks. Then take your findings to the craft table to fancy them up with paint. Acrylics work great for this project.

For activities that span the hour, the two-step Make & Play approach works well. You may want to do a little prep the day before to make it easier, like putting crafting necessities into one small bin that you can pull out to surprise the kids.

According to recent reports, 19. Wage war. Ah, the classic card game that is so simple to learn and so hard to win. It is possible that a game of war can take longer than one hour, but it rarely takes less. You do two card battles with the highest card the winner until one person has all the cards. Get the complete rules here.

Industry observers note that 20. Create a mini catapult. Little Bins for Little Hands has an awesome tutorial, using craft sticks and other office supplies you’re sure to have around the house. Once it’s built, set up target practice plates before letting the marshmallows fly.

In a recent development, 21. Put on a show. Puppets never get old; they’re easy to make with an old sock, brown paper lunch bag, or even familiar characters glued to craft sticks. Whatever method you choose, spend time creating and playing with puppets when you’ve got an hour or more to spare. Be sure to stock the craft bin with all kinds of googly eyes, buttons, yarn, and doo-dads to help bring your buddies to life. Then find an old sheet or use a baby’s blanket draped over the table to create a stage. Bravo!

According to recent reports, it’s that time again. Yup, your Elf on the Shelf is about to parachute in to make your life (slightly) more challenging for the next few weeks. Get ahead of the game and prep your bag of tricks with these brilliant ideas. From Elf on the Shelf clothes to last-minute Elf on the Shelf ideas that’ll make the whole family giggle, we’ve got enough easy Elf ideas to last you the entire holiday season.

In a recent development, I remember when my kids were little, and they got their first elves. Not going to lie, remembering to move the thing every night was a struggle. But when I made the effort and managed to pull off even the easiest of Elf ideas, the look in their eyes was priceless.

It has been revealed that 1. Elf held captive. If you have two Scout elves, this easy Elf idea is a lot of fun. Pull out a toy train and a string, and decide which elf is going to be extra naughty by tying up the other one.

Sources indicate that 2. Proposal a hot cocoa party. This is fun on the first night or maybe on a weekend day. Get mugs, instant cocoa, and marshmallows set up in advance and settle the elves against the mugs. Snag printables for the party here.

3. Spell it out. Do you have Scrabble tiles or Bananagrams? Then it’s a cinch to let your elf leave a sweet message for your littles to discover the next day.

4. Caught in the act. With this easy elf idea, you’ll use a bag of M&Ms, chocolate chips, or even a box of sugar cereal, and position your elf with its backside out of the bag.

5. Exhausted elf. All those trips up to the North Pole make for one tired elf. Let your little one in red take a day off. Make them a little bed with a doll blanket and a cotton ball for a pillow.

Industry observers note that 6. Deeds worth doing. Since reporting good deeds to Santa is your elf’s duty, it’s the perfect opportunity to remind kids about the spirit of Christmas. We dig the free downloadable from Over the Massive Moon.

It has been revealed that 7. Elf spaghetti. Whip up Buddy the Elf’s favorite dish for your little helper. Hint: this is a great idea for the night you make pasta. You’ll also need syrup (of course), marshmallows, candy, and chocolate syrup. Find out how to make a batch over at Instructables.

8. Riding the banister. Those naughty elves are always looking for an adrenaline rush! Use a Frisbee and sticky tape to get your little buddy set up at the top and ready to ride.

9. Sitting pretty. Have your elf take a seat inside your wreath or on the holiday table for a picture-perfect spot.

10. Play games. Set up your elf mid-move with this adorable mini-Twister printable.

Sources indicate that 11. Window view. If you’ve got a window and a curtain rod, you’ve got a sweet spot to hang your elf. Easy-peasy.

Sources indicate that 12. Rock climbing wall. All you need is several pre-made bows to make a route for your elf.

13. Coloring elf. Take 30 seconds to scribble in a coloring book or on a printable, scatter crayons, and set up your elf. Giggles are guaranteed!

It has been revealed that 15. Zipline. This Elf on the Shelf idea is popular, but it does take a little time to set up. All you need is string or yarn, a candy cane, and a way to secure your elf to the candy cane!

16. LEGO throne. Whether you use DUPLO or LEGO, making a seat for Santa’s little helper can be done in less than five minutes.

17. Elf in the kitchen. Got a play kitchen? Then let your elf whip up something yummy.

18. On the road. With a toy car, your elf can go just about anywhere they want to go. Headed to buy a Christmas tree? Done. Want to take Wonder Woman out on a date? Totally!

19. Play Picasso. A dry-erase marker, a family photo, and a sense of humor are all you need. Give your kids beards and cat ears: See how much they laugh!

Sources indicate that 20. Put the elf in the freezer. Your elf sure does miss the North Pole! Give him a little time to chill.

21. Toilet paper tricks. Add an elf to a roll of toilet paper and send them down the stairs. Don’t have a second level? Leave a trail of written messages down the hall instead.

In a recent development, 22. Bath time. You don’t need a Barbie bath to let your Elf soak aching bones— a plastic bowl or storage container will do the trick. Add marshmallows for bubbles, and you’re set.

23. Gone fishing. Your kids will love waking up to find the elf “fishing” for goldfish crackers in the bathroom sink.

Recent findings suggest that 24. Story time. Position the elf with a favorite holiday book and a captivated audience.

Sources indicate that 25. Hanging by a limb. Any elf will feel right at home when dangling from a branch of the Christmas tree.

26. Spa day. Wrap your elf in a paper towel, give them cucumber eye patches, and just like that, it’s a spa day.

Sources indicate that 27. Puzzle play. Settling your elf in for the night with a puzzle is easy and fun.

In a recent development, 28. Paper bag race. Take those lunch bags that have been cluttering your drawer and collect a few stuffies. Then, stage a sack race-style scene across your dining room table or kitchen island.

Sources indicate that 29. Elfie selfie. Position your elf in front of the family laptop and snap a picture. Just be forewarned, if it’s a laptop you use, you’ll need to get it set back up before the kids get home from school.

30. Sweet snow angels. It’s not quite as cold down here as it is at the North Pole. When your elf gets antsy for chilly weather, make them a personal snow angel. You can use flour (but it’s messy), sprinkles, or rice, which is my personal favorite because it’s the easiest to clean up!

Recent findings suggest that 31. All wrapped up. Give your elf the scissors, tape, and wrapping paper. Scatter shredded paper and tape around, and it’ll be like they were caught in the act of wrapping up Santa’s gifts!

It has been revealed that 32. Elf making popcorn. Someone’s ready for family movie night!

33. Don’t move the elf. Well, it looks like your kids were so well-behaved that no North Pole reporting was needed. It’s also the perfect excuse for one of those nights you forget to move them.

34. Cards, anyone? Didn’t you know elves love to play games? They do, and they love to be caught mid-game.

35. A Stuck Elf. This is a super-easy elf idea, and you don’t even need the message board to pull it off. Just grab a mason jar or an empty water bottle and a prominent place to display your elf’s tight situation.

In a recent development, 36. S’more to love. Some toothpicks, roasted marshmallows, chocolate squares, graham crackers, and tea lights are all you need to set up this cozy and easy elf idea.

37. Read all about it. Prop them up on a favorite Christmas story or beloved book.

38. Caught red-handed. Have your elf stage a scene of questionable actions and tape up the area with crepe paper.

39. Photo editor. They can’t help but make mischief, and marking up a festive photo is a silly way to say, “Elf wuz here.”.

40. Riding dinos. If you’ve got a plastic dinosaur (T. rex preferred), then you’ve got what you need to give your elf a prehistoric ride.

According to recent reports, 41. Send the Elf back to the North Pole. Possibly one of our favorite easy elf ideas: on Christmas Morning, make sure they’re out of sight, and of course, leave a note.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we can already feel the tension spreading through our bodies: It’s time to put away the iPad, but there is a small person who is almost certainly going to lose their mind when you tell them. Whether you resort to a countdown timer or go the “this is your last show” route, it’s pretty much always a struggle.

Industry observers note that perhaps you need a new strategy. Parenting coach Dr. Chelsey Hauge-Zavaleta recently shared her method for successfully ending iPad time, and it combines a little bit of the two approaches above with some voice modulation and sensory input.

A few things to note about this method. Using language like “We have one more song” instead of “This is our last song before we leave for school” focuses on what the child is doing now versus what you are doing in the future. It’s easier for kids to accept the transition this way.

Sources indicate that “Melodic intonation” is when you use a sing-songy voice to make a statement. It helps kids notice what you are saying and acknowledge it. Take a look at Miss Rachel and a lot of the other preschool-focused programming, and you’ll see it employed often. Using melodic intonation for the phrase “iPad is all done” helps to signal the transition for the child.

Recent findings suggest that it’s important to remember that even when using a technique like this, it will take you doing it the same way over and over several times before your child catches on and gets with the program. If they have a meltdown, don’t engage; stay calm; and move on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you don’t give a toddler something to do, they’ll find their own source of entertainment—and that can be a terrifying prospect (you know the feeling if you’ve suddenly noticed the house is too quiet only to find that they’ve somehow given themselves bangs). To keep them out of trouble and thoroughly entertained, we’ve rounded up some awesome games for toddlers that are sure to be a hit, whether you’re indoors or outdoors. The best part? Your kiddo won’t know it, but they offer ample opportunities for hands-on learning. Ready for endless fun? On your mark. Get set. Go find your tot’s new fave!

It has been revealed that toddlers are bundles of energy: always on the move, always growing, always learning. Learning with play is essential for their development because it improves small and large motor skills, muscle strength, emotional intelligence, language development, spatial awareness, and more. According to an article by Michael Yogman, MD, FAAP, on Healthychildren.org, “research demonstrates play can improve children’s abilities to plan, organize, get along with others, and regulate emotions. In addition, play helps with language, math, and social skills, and even helps children cope with stress.”.

Figuring out how to keep toddlers engaged is no easy feat. There are outdoor games, indoor games, toys, beginner board games… You get the idea. The key is to decide which activity is right for your kiddo, and that depends on factors like their age, energy level, developmental stage, and other milestones.

One of the most important things to consider is what interests your toddler. Do they love Ms. Rachel? Are they obsessed with a sport? Do they love baby dolls or animals? Once you figure out what will keep them interested, you can go from there.

Another factor is something called Play Schemas, a concept first used by Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget. As stated in My Play Cupboard, Play Schemas are repeated patterns of behaviour you notice children engaging in when they play. Nine schemas can be commonly observed in young children, including connection, transforming, enveloping, enclosing, and positioning.

Once you figure out which Play Schema your toddler is drawn to, that will help you decide what type of games they’ll enjoy the most.

Industry observers note that give your jumping bean something to jump about—letters! We love that this outdoor game from The Imagination Tree combines alphabet awareness with the chance to get those wiggles out. Simply write letters in sidewalk chalk and have your little one hop from one to another as you call them out. And all you need to get started is a set of sidewalk chalk. Read all about it and check out the phonics and math variations over at The Imagination Tree.

Recent findings suggest that let your toddler be your boss with a few rounds of Simon Says. Toddlers love the chance to be in charge! Then, you can give the commands for a bit. It's silly, active, and engaging—that's why it's an early childhood classic. Plus, it gives little ones a chance to practice following instructions, taking turns, and building listening skills. Simon Says go play!

Industry observers note that toddlers love climbing under, over, and on top of all sorts of things. Obstacle courses let you take that natural climbing instinct and make it a game. Build an indoor obstacle course with painters' tape, making lines for your little one to walk on top of and jump over. Or take the fun outside and challenge them to stay off the grass in the yard or the wood chips at the playground. Ready for a bonus round? Turn the obstacle course game into follow-the-leader and take turns being the leader. Check out this post for even more obstacle course fun.

It has been revealed that kids of all ages love a good scavenger hunt. Send your toddler on a hunt through the house for four red things or two things with wheels. In a recent development, try the dress-up challenge: give your toddler a scenario or career, like summertime, rainy day, forest animal friends, sports star, or construction worker, and send them off to create an outfit that meets that challenge. We guarantee that you'll get lots of fantastic photos out of this game! It's also great to play after dinner to encourage little ones to put on their PJs. Last challenge: bedtime!

Sources indicate that most board games are still a little tricky for young toddlers—but Where's Bear from Peaceable Kingdom is just right. Little ones get to play hide-and-seek with little bear, stack the sturdy cardboard blocks, and learn upcoming words as they play.

It has been revealed that caught waiting in line or at a restaurant without a stocked bag of goodies? Then pull out the animal guessing game, a game we love because it requires no gear. Think of an animal and ask questions until your game playing buddy guesses it. Does it have legs? Does it live in a tree? Older twos and three-year-olds love this game. When you're playing with younger toddlers, change it to the animal sounds game: make a sound (MOOO!) and have the toddler guess what kind of animal makes that noise. Then switch it up and have them make the sound.

It has been revealed that your toddler will spend lots of time spelling their name and piecing together words with this Magnetic Rainbow Busy Box from Mama.Papa.Bubba. It can be an art project just to create the box and they'll have endless fun learning and spelling once it's finished.

What are the benefits of toddler games?

Playing games with your toddler is not only a great opportunity to enjoy quality time with your child, but they help develop important life skills like problem solving, small and large motor skills, physical coordination, hand-eye coordination, and learning how to be social with others.

What types of games are best for toddlers?

While it depends on your child’s age, interests, and development, the best toddler games are simple and fun. Popular ideas include pretend play, memory games, music games, and basic movements, like a simplified version of Simon Says.

How much screen time is appropriate for toddlers?

According to the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry, toddlers should have very limited daily screen time.

In a recent development, there are online toddler games that are designed specifically for young children. Parents should always review the game or content before allowing their child to watch, monitor usage, and opt for an ad-free, child-friendly tablet or platform.

What are some fun indoor games for toddlers?

Toddler indoor games should be fun and easy to set up: memory, obstacle courses, block building challenges, sensory stations, and pretend play like “the floor is lava,” “vet clinic,” and “grocery store.”.

Latest Update: Why You Should Fight the Urge to Make a Happy Kid Happier

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We are walking between two tractors in a barn when I say something very stupid to my 22-month-old son.
  • And then I decide to say, “Do you think the cat is in here today?”.
  • In a recent development, last time we were here in the fall, there was a big, gray cat who got just close enough so that my toddler could bend down, reach out the tips of his fingers, and briefly graze its arched back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We are walking between two tractors in a barn when I say something very stupid to my 22-month-old son. We’ve been at this farm for about an hour, the kind of place where you can reach your fingers through the fence to pet the goats and stare into the pigpen and marvel at how much bigger pigs are than you think. It’s a mysteriously warm winter day, and my son has thrown his jacket off, his stroller discarded somewhere around the sheep pen. For the first time in months, we are feeling the sun on our faces. He’s having the time of his life. He’s already pet a one-day-old lamb and has discovered that in the barn we are at the moment walking through there’s not one, not two, but three tractors.

And then I decide to say, “Do you think the cat is in here today?”.

In a recent development, last time we were here in the fall, there was a big, gray cat who got just close enough so that my toddler could bend down, reach out the tips of his fingers, and briefly graze its arched back. But that was enough. He’d brought up the cat for days, and I knew if he saw it again, he’d be so, so happy.

Recent findings suggest that except there was one problem. The cat wasn’t here.

Why did I have to mention the cat? It was a perfect moment; we were like an illustration from a children’s picture book. But now, there was only one thing my son wanted to do: find the cat. I’d reminded him that there was a cat. And he loves cats. Especially this cat, the famed cat that let him touch its fur for a fraction of a second. So of course, in a very cat-like fashion, the cat was nowhere to be found.

According to recent reports, that’s when the tears began. The three tractors were no longer enough. The baby goats—garbage. The teeny tiny lambs, only minutes ago, he was thrilled to pet. Who needs them? It was only the cat now.

Sources indicate that “I don’t know,” I stated, hoping his outburst wasn’t calling too much attention to us from the less cat-obsessed farm visitors. “He’s probably sleeping somewhere.”.

“WHERE CAT,” he demanded, over and over again.

And just like that, I’d broken my own biggest rule of parenting: Never try to make a happy kid happier.

This rule came to me via my friend Joanna, who had learned it from her parents. As soon as she told me, I knew she’d identified one of my greatest weaknesses as a parent. I always want my son to be having a good time, and there’s some part of me that worries if I’m not actively trying to make his time better, it’s not as good as it could be.

As a baby, if he was enjoying gnawing on a particular teether, I’d jump in to give him another one, too. Oh, he likes the dog at this park? Let’s leave this park with one dog to find a dog park full of dogs. If he were having a perfectly nice time throwing rocks in a puddle, I’d offer to find him better rocks that would make an even bigger splash.

There’s an impulse in us as parents not just to nurture, to make sure all gaps are closed. We want to provide the complete package for our kids, to make sure all their needs are met in the best possible way. And that urge is good. It’s why we don’t abandon them in the woods when they won’t stop crying at 4 a.m. and why we keep feeding them every day even when they throw everything we offer on the floor. But it also means we can fail to notice when we aren’t needed.

According to recent reports, what “don’t make a happy kid happier” does is remind me that sometimes, just being happy is enough. Kids live in a world of the immediate now, where whatever they are doing is often the only thing on their minds. Yes, there might be bigger, splashier rocks to throw in the puddle, but the rocks they have in their hand suit them just fine. What I think I’m doing when I do this is helping my son, but what I’m actually doing is pointing out that what he’s doing might not be good enough. Suddenly he can see that the emperor has no clothes, and it actually becomes not good enough.

According to recent reports, we never did find the cat. But I paid the price for my misstep in toddler currency: a temper tantrum. He settled down eventually, and by the time we left the farm, he was happily kicking and chatting in his stroller. I thought about stopping for ice cream at the gift shop, but I decided against it this time. He was just fine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that abdulrahman El Bahnasawy, 28, of Ontario, Canada, was sentenced today to 50 years in prison for offenses related to a 2020 attack on correctional officers at U.S. Penitentiary Allenwood. This sentence will run consecutive to the 40-year sentence he is at the moment serving for his role in plotting a mass-casualty terrorist attack in New York City on behalf of ISIS.

Recent findings suggest that “Bahnasawy, who is already serving a 40-year sentence in federal prison for plotting mass casualty attacks in Latest York City on behalf of ISIS, savagely attacked corrections officers once again on behalf of ISIS,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “Today’s sentence will further ensure that Bahnasawy remains in prison, where he can do much less harm, for a very long time.”.

“We will prosecute those who aid, attempt to aid, or commit violence on behalf of the pernicious ISIS ideology wherever they may be found,” stated U.S. Attorney Brian D. Miller for the Middle District of Pennsylvania. “Today’s sentence reflects our unwavering commitment to fight those who perpetrate violence in the name of ISIS even behind prison walls.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Although he was behind bars, this convicted terrorist committed a horrific attack on two corrections officers in the name of ISIS, which they fortunately survived,” mentioned Assistant Director Jarod Brown of the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division. “Today’s sentencing highlights that violent attacks by those who support the evil ideology of ISIS or other foreign terrorist organizations cannot be tolerated by our society. Fighting terrorism is a central part of the FBI’s mission to protect the American people, and the FBI is committed to working with our law enforcement partners to hold these vicious criminals accountable.”.

In a recent development, bahnasawy was an inmate at USP Allenwood who, on Dec. 7, 2020, attacked two corrections officers using a weapon made from part of a steel desk in his cell. Bahnasawy stabbed one officer in the head and face, and, when a second responded to assist, Bahnasawy stabbed her in the hand.

The first officer eventually lost his right eye as a result of the attack. When Bahnasawy was restrained, a note was found in his sock that read, “This is a terrorist attack for the Islamic State.” A pledge of allegiance to the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham (ISIS) was also found taped to the inside of a locker door in Bahnasawy’s prison cell. Bahnasawy pleaded guilty in November 2025 to multiple counts of assault, assault with intent to commit murder, and possession of contraband inside a prison as well as providing material support to ISIS, a designated foreign terrorist organization.

At the time of the attacks at USP Allenwood, Bahnasawy was serving a 40-year sentence for his role in plotting a mass-casualty terrorist attack in Latest York City on behalf of ISIS. Bahnasawy, a then-20-year-old Canadian citizen and resident, plotted with Talha Haroon and Russell Salic to conduct bombings and shootings in heavily populated areas of New York City during the Islamic holy month of Ramadhan in 2016, all in the name of ISIS.

An undercover FBI agent (UC) infiltrated the co-conspirators’ terrorist plot, posing as an ISIS supporter prepared to join in the attacks. The FBI arrested Bahnasawy in May 2016 after he traveled from Canada to the Upcoming York City area in preparation for the attacks, and he has been in custody since that time.

This case was investigated by the FBI’s Philadelphia Field Office.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Geoffrey MacArthur for the Middle District of Pennsylvania and Deputy Chief Larry Schneider of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section prosecuted the case.

Breaking: Justice Department Confirms Results from Operation Not Forgotten 2026

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1349 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fbi

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Department of Justice and FBI announced today results of the personnel surge in support of Operation Not Forgotten 2026, which focuses on unresolved cases in Indian country with a priority on cases involving violence against women and children, including those who are missing or murdered.
  • In its fourth year, Operation Not Forgotten surged personnel and investigative resources across the country from April 1 through September 30, resulting in 118 arrests, 41 individuals charged federally, 25 child victims identified or located, and 72 weapons recovered.
  • “The Department of Justice will always work to deliver justice for the victims of violent crime in Indian country,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Department of Justice and FBI announced today results of the personnel surge in support of Operation Not Forgotten 2026, which focuses on unresolved cases in Indian country with a priority on cases involving violence against women and children, including those who are missing or murdered.

In its fourth year, Operation Not Forgotten surged personnel and investigative resources across the country from April 1 through September 30, resulting in 118 arrests, 41 individuals charged federally, 25 child victims identified or located, and 72 weapons recovered. FBI agents conducted 990 interviews and 232 search operations. Arrests increased by 123% and subjects charged by 52% over 2025.

“The Department of Justice will always work to deliver justice for the victims of violent crime in Indian country,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Thanks to the hard work of the FBI, our U.S. Attorneys, and other federal and tribal partners, Operation Not Forgotten and Operation Steadfast Promise are helping make communities safer and providing comfort for victims and families.”.

Industry observers note that “This year’s Operation Not Forgotten continued this FBI’s largest commitment to Indian Country in the history of the Bureau,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “The results were outstanding – from April 1 through September 30, this FBI worked more than 500 cases, a 59% increase from last year’s operation; 118 arrests, a 123% increase; and 41 subjects charged federally, a 52% increase. This is in addition to 25 child victims identified or located and 72 weapons recovered. These involved life-saving operations, with cases including child sexual abuse, physical assault and abuse, domestic violence, CSAM cases, and more.

In a recent development, “Operation Not Forgotten sends a loud and clear message that our long-forgotten partners in Indian Country are forgotten no more,” said Director Patel. “When I assumed the position of FBI Director a year and a half ago, this FBI promised we would be there for our tribal partners. We have and will continue to be – through our 400 agents dedicated to Indian country, 30 Safe Trails Task Forces, and increased awareness with our Voices Not Forgotten program, where the FBI quadrupled the rewards to at least $25,000 for information associated with homicides, kidnappings and missing persons in Indian country. Thank you to our federal, state, and local partners who continue to work with us to ensure these unsolved crimes and cases receive the surge in resources they deserve.”.

“Operation Not Forgotten demonstrates the Trump Administration’s commitment to protecting tribal communities, strengthening public safety, and ensuring that victims and their families have access to justice,” said Billy Kirkland, Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs, U.S. Department of the Interior. “Through close collaboration across the federal government and in partnership with tribal, state, and local law enforcement, we are bringing additional resources and investigative support to Indian Country to address violent crime, advance unresolved cases, and help families find answers. The Department of the Interior, through the Bureau of Indian Affairs, remains committed to working alongside our partners to deliver meaningful results and build safer communities for generations to come.".

Examples of cases charged during this period include:.

In the District of Wyoming, the surge resulted in the federal indictment of 18 individuals for an array of violent crimes, and child abuse offenses on the Wind River Indian Reservation, including U.S. v. Jose Benito Ocon: This prosecution arises from an August 2025 incident near Riverton, where the defendant allegedly executed a male passenger with a gunshot to the head inside a moving vehicle before turning the firearm on two female witnesses. Leveraging the surge’s enhanced investigative assets, a grand jury returned an indictment charging the defendant with five felony counts, including first-degree murder, discharging a firearm during a crime of violence, and two distinct counts of assault with a dangerous weapon. He faces a mandatory sentence of life imprisonment if convicted. In U.S. v. Darlynn Sheree Seminole, federal prosecutors filed charges following a June 2026 domestic violence intervention by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) Wind River Police Department, involving allegations of severe physical trauma inflicted on a 10-year-old.

In the District of Nevada, in July a federal grand jury returned a superseding indictment charging Delshay Astor with the alleged murder of Anna Scott, a member of the Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe, on the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony in February 2022, and also charged Joel Christy for assisting Astor to avoid apprehension.

In the District of Minnesota, Operation Not Forgotten has resulted in four cases charged during the surge period with violent and sexual offenses in Indian Country, including sexual abuse of minors, domestic assault causing substantial bodily injury, assault by strangulation, and assault with intent to commit kidnapping. One recent case includes U.S. v. Courtney John Barrett Sr. indicted on September 22, 2026, on two counts of sexual abuse of a minor.

Industry observers note that in the District of Montana, Michael Plentybuffalo was charged in the death of Shann Nomee, who went missing during an extreme cold snap in January 2024 and whose frozen body was found in a field north of Lodge Grass, Montana after a community led search and a tip to the Bureau of Indian Affairs that pointed to Plentybuffalo. His case is pending trial.

Also in Montana, Lance Crookedarm was charged with the May 2026 violent assault and non-fatal strangulation of a female victim.

In the District of Arizona, at least four cases were charged including two violent assaults, an arson, and the aggravated sexual abuse of a minor under 12, all of which occurred on the Navajo Nation, as well as an additional assault that was committed on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation.

FBI’s Operation Steadfast Promise.

Operation Steadfast Promise, first revealed in 2026, is a continuing comprehensive surge of resources to address a wide range of violent criminal threats impacting Indian country. Operation Steadfast Promise builds on the successes of Operation Not Forgotten with the addition of multiple latest initiatives to improve public safety in Tribal communities. The FBI, in coordination with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices, the Bureau of Indian Affairs Missing and Murdered Unit, Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and Tribal and other federal law enforcement partners, is working across multiple territories to bring investigative aid to cases and resolution for victims and their families. Since Operation Steadfast Promise began in April, the FBI opened over 1,200 new investigations in Indian country, obtained criminal charges on 678 subjects, made over 700 arrests, recovered 2,260 weapons, and made 140 drug seizures.

This year, Operation Not Forgotten continued to address the over 4,000 open investigations in Indian country including death investigations, child abuse cases, domestic violence, and adult sexual abuse investigations, underscoring the persistent and urgent need for sustained resource investment in these communities.

During Operation Not Forgotten, the FBI surged personnel, including investigative, intelligence, and other support personnel, on rotating temporary duty assignments across Indian country in twelve FBI field offices, in Albuquerque, Billings, Detroit, Denver, Jackson, Las Vegas, Minneapolis, Oklahoma City, Omaha, Portland, Phoenix and Salt Lake City. Working in close coordination with Tribal law enforcement agencies, the BIA Missing and Murdered Unit, and U.S. Attorneys' Offices, together law enforcement worked to advance open investigations and pursue accountability for victims and their families.

Additionally, the FBI has brought focus to a new FBI’s Voices Not Forgotten webpage that includes a searchable and interactive map that brings attention to FBI investigations in Indian country where the FBI, in coordination with state, local and Tribal law enforcement are seeking the public’s assistance. In August 2026, the FBI announced the establishment of a new protocol which created a minimum reward of up to $25,000 for all publicly advertised cases involving homicides, kidnappings and missing persons in Indian country where the FBI has assumed jurisdiction.

The FBI remains committed to standing alongside Tribal communities, federal partners, and local law enforcement to address the violent crime threats that continue to impact Indian country. To learn more, visit www.fbi.gov/investigate/violent-crime/indian-country-crime.

The FBI encourages anyone with information related to unresolved violent crimes in Indian country to contact their local FBI field office or submit a tip at https://tips.fbi.gov.

8 Essentials for Your Family's First Trip to Disney World

📅 03 Jan 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moms

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
